verdict.summary: You create a GitHub OAuth app from your account settings and it works as soon as you click Register application. GitHub's registration docs describe no review, verification or test-user stage. The main work is picking narrow scopes and deciding whether your integration can handle access tokens that expire after 8 hours.
verdict.approval_wait: none (no review step is documented for OAuth apps; GitHub Marketplace listing was not researched)

steps.title: Decide between an OAuth app and a GitHub App
steps.detail: GitHub recommends a GitHub App for new integrations because it uses fine-grained permissions and can act as itself. This guide covers OAuth apps, which is what Composio's GitHub OAUTH2 auth config uses. Choose an OAuth app if you want user-scoped access through Composio.

steps.title: Open the New OAuth App form
steps.detail: Sign in to GitHub and click your profile picture > Settings > Developer settings. In the left sidebar, click OAuth apps, then click New OAuth App.

steps.title: Enter the app name and homepage
steps.detail: In "Application name", enter the name users will see on the consent screen. In "Homepage URL", enter the full URL of your app's website. "Application description" is optional.

steps.title: Set the authorization callback URL
steps.detail: In "Authorization callback URL", paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config. GitHub compares the redirect_uri in each authorization request with this URL, so it must match exactly. You can add up to 10 callback URLs.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: A trailing slash or wrong host will cause a redirect_uri mismatch error.

steps.title: Choose the device flow and token expiry settings
steps.detail: Only check Enable Device Flow if you will use device authorization. "Expire user access tokens" is on by default: access tokens then expire after 8 hours, and every refresh returns a new refresh token. Turn it off only if your integration cannot refresh tokens yet.
gotchas: If you leave expiry on, store each new refresh token after every refresh. The old one is replaced.
Refresh tokens expire after 6 months without use.

steps.title: Register the app and copy the credentials
steps.detail: Click Register application. Copy the Client ID and create a client secret on the app's settings page. Store the secret securely.

steps.title: Choose a narrow scope list
steps.detail: Composio's default list (repo, user, gist, notifications, project, workflow, codespace) is broad. repo grants full read/write access to all public and private repositories, and workflow can change GitHub Actions workflow files. Keep only the scopes your agent needs; for profile-only access, read:user is enough. Write the scopes as a space-separated list.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config with your credentials
steps.detail: In Composio, create a GitHub auth config that uses your own OAuth app (not the managed one). Enter your Client ID, Client Secret and the narrowed scopes. Composio uses https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize and https://github.com/login/oauth/access_token as the authorization and token URLs.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection from Composio and approve it on GitHub's consent screen. Check that the redirect comes back to Composio without a redirect_uri error and that an API call works. If your client sends PKCE, code_challenge must be a 43-character SHA-256 hash, with code_verifier sent at the token exchange.

steps.title: Open the app to other users
steps.detail: No submission is needed. GitHub's registration docs describe no review or verification for OAuth apps, so any GitHub user can authorize once the app is registered. Separately, check whether your users' organizations restrict third-party OAuth app access.

requirements.detail: Both are required fields on the registration form. The description is optional.

requirements.item: Authorization callback URL matching Composio's callback
requirements.detail: The redirect_uri in each request must match a registered callback URL. Up to 10 are allowed.

requirements.item: Refresh-token handling if token expiry is enabled
requirements.detail: Access tokens expire after 8 hours, and each refresh rotates the refresh token.

scopes.effect: Full read/write access to public and private repositories, including code. Very broad, but no review is required; request it only if needed.
Read access to the user's profile. A good minimal scope.
Can add and update GitHub Actions workflow files. High-impact write access; no review tier.
Write access to gists. Included in Composio's defaults; drop it if unused.

blockers.symptom: The redirect_uri error page appears on GitHub during authorization
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri sent in the request does not match the app's registered callback URL.
blockers.fix: Paste the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config into "Authorization callback URL" in the OAuth app settings.

blockers.symptom: The connection stops working after about 8 hours, or months later
blockers.cause: With "Expire user access tokens" on, access tokens expire after 8 hours. Refresh tokens rotate on every refresh and expire after 6 months without use.
blockers.fix: Make sure refresh is handled and the newest refresh token is stored after each refresh, or turn off token expiry in the app settings.

composio.note: Composio's managed GitHub OAuth app is enough for quick testing. Callbacks go through Composio's backend. Register your own OAuth app when you want your own client ID/secret, your own branding on the consent screen, or a narrower scope list than Composio's broad defaults. Because GitHub has no review step for OAuth apps, switching to your own app costs about 15 minutes.

open_questions: Whether organization owners must approve OAuth app access to org repositories (third-party access restrictions) was not researched. This could block users from reaching org repos.
GitHub Marketplace listing review was not researched. It is only relevant if you want a Marketplace listing.
No rate limits or install caps for new OAuth apps were found.
The 'project' and 'user' scope definitions were not individually verified.
Probes of github.com endpoints timed out, so the authorize and token URLs are confirmed only by Composio's catalog and GitHub's docs, not by a live probe.
Token expiry and refresh behavior may differ for older apps created before the 'Expire user access tokens' option existed.
